note: Mostly judgment-shaped. Two mechanical seams are assertable (Entity Trap detection, conjunction test) plus one behavioural check (pushing back on granularity before offering a saga). The correct decomposition of a domain has many valid answers and is not asserted.

evals.name: detects-entity-trap
evals.prompt: Here's the component breakdown my team came up with for the new logistics platform: ShipmentManager, CarrierManager, RouteEngine, DriverController, InvoiceProcessor, TrackingHandler. Does this look reasonable before we start building?
evals.expected_output: Flags all six as Entity Trap suffixes, explains the three failure modes (ambiguous names, dumping grounds, too coarse-grained), and proposes action-named replacements derived from what each would actually do. Should also note the honest exception — if this is genuinely CRUD over entities it needs a framework, not an architecture.

assertions.text: Identifies the Manager/Engine/Controller/Processor/Handler suffixes as the tell for the Entity Trap
Explains at least two of the three failure modes: names state no role, components become dumping grounds, components grow too coarse-grained
Proposes replacement component names based on actions performed rather than entities managed

evals.name: applies-the-conjunction-test
evals.prompt: Can you sanity check this component? Here's what it's responsible for: 'The Enrollment component is responsible for validating the student application and checking prerequisite completion, and it also assigns the student to a cohort, as well as generating the tuition invoice. In addition it emails the welcome packet and provisions the student's LMS account.'
evals.expected_output: Runs the conjunction test, identifies each 'and'/'also'/'as well as'/'in addition' as marking a responsibility that belongs elsewhere, and extracts them into separate components — leaving validation and prerequisite checking in Enrollment and moving cohort assignment, invoicing, notification and account provisioning out.

assertions.text: Explicitly identifies the conjunctive phrases (and / also / as well as / in addition) as the signal of too much responsibility
Proposes at least three separate components extracted from the trailing clauses
Produces a rewritten responsibility statement for the original component that reads as a single responsibility

evals.name: pushes-back-before-offering-a-saga
evals.prompt: We split our booking flow into four microservices — reserve-inventory, take-payment, issue-ticket, send-confirmation. Problem is we need all four to succeed or none of them. What's the best saga pattern for coordinating this?
evals.expected_output: Should not answer the saga question first. Treats the need for a cross-service transaction as evidence the granularity is wrong, and proposes merging the services that must transact together before reaching for a compensating-transaction framework. Only after that should it describe the saga option, with the double-failure caveat.

assertions.text: Identifies the need for a transaction spanning services as a granularity problem before recommending any saga pattern
Proposes merging the services that must participate in the atomic transaction as the primary fix
Presents the saga as conditional on the services genuinely needing different architecture characteristics, not as the default answer
Notes that compensating updates can themselves fail and the design must account for it
